approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package of three bills that would let the Commonwealth impose charges for indirect biosecurity services funded by future cost-recovery arrangements.

The package would amend three Imposition Acts to create a legal structure supporting cost recovery for activities such as scientific analysis, intelligence and surveillance under the Biosecurity Bill.
The bill itself is enabling and does not set charge amounts, which would be prescribed in delegated legislation, and would have no direct financial impacts on businesses.
Amends the Quarantine Charges (Imposition – Excise) Act 2014.
Allows the Commonwealth to impose charges for prescribed matters connected with administering the Biosecurity Bill.
Enables cost recovery for indirect biosecurity services where the charge is a duty of excise under section 55 of the Constitution.
Users of the biosecurity system and businesses that may be liable for charges set in delegated legislation.

Introduced the Quarantine Charges (Imposition-Excise) Amendment Bill 2014, the third of three charging bills supporting the Biosecurity Bill package, which will impose charges only when they are considered a duty of excise.

Summed up the Biosecurity Bill debate, noting the Quarantine Act has been amended more than 50 times over 106 years and Australia's agricultural production was worth $53 billion in 2013 to 2014, and assured the House the Inspector-General of Biosecurity position and its funding, currently held by Dr Michael Bond, will continue.
